ToTape9.what: Airwindows' most complete tape emulation: tape saturation, flutter, head bump and a built-in loudness clipper.
ToTape9.sound: Huge, deep and raw. Soaks up highs like real tape and thickens bass; with the output pushed it clips hard but stays clean on most material.
ToTape9.use: Putting a whole mix or buss 'to tape', gentle warmth or heavy slam, and as a loudness maximizer in one plugin.

controls.Tilt: Leans the tone brighter or darker, like a tape-machine calibration.
controls.Shape: Old-school sonority at one end, big-studio smoothness at the other.
controls.Flutter: Amount of tape speed wobble. 0 is off.
controls.Bias: Tape bias. A touch of overbias tames tizzy highs.
controls.Output: Level into the final clip stage. 0.5 just touches it; higher clips harder, lower leaves pure tape.

TapeHack2.what: A tape-compression 'hack': a slew-limited filter that stops highs getting louder, a step up from TapeHack.
TapeHack2.sound: Tape-like squash of the highs without added grit. Smooth, big and dense rather than distorted. Not a literal tape emulation.
TapeHack2.use: Fattening and glueing drums, mixes or busses, or as the saturation stage in a console chain.

ToTape8.what: ToTape with simple gain staging, optimised Dubly and a safety clipper.
ToTape8.sound: Clean, level-soaking tape. Dubly cancels harmonics, giving the 'clean level compressor' feel of real machines, with a lively Seventies midrange.
ToTape8.use: Tracks and the mix buss when you want tape character without wrecking the tone.

controls.Tilt: Balances Dubly encode against decode. Centre is musical; 1.0 is the studio encode trick, 0.0 decode only.
controls.Shape: Midrange character: searing and compressed, or dark and vibey.
controls.Flutter: Amount of tape speed wobble. 0 is off.
controls.Output: Level after the tape and before the final clipper. About 0.4 leaves tape only.

ToTape7.what: ToTape with bias and full Dubly encode/decode controls.
ToTape7.sound: Gritty, fierce and flexible. Soaks up loudness well and has a built-in clipper. Matching Dubly settings sounds normal; mismatching them colours the mids.
ToTape7.use: Sound design and tailoring your own tape tone. Set everything to the middle for a normal sound.

controls.EncAmt: Dubly encode amount: brightened, compressed boost before the tape.
controls.TapeDrv: Tape drive. 0.5 is unity gain; raise it for more saturation.
controls.Flutter: Tape speed wobble. 0.5 is realistic, 0 is off.
controls.Bias: Tape bias. Slight overbias is best against tizzy highs.
controls.HeadBmp: Head bump. 0.5 is the most realistic; lower returns the original bass, higher exaggerates it.
controls.DecAmt: Dubly decode amount: undoes the encode and smooths the saturation.

ToTape6.what: Airwindows tape emulation for 2020: deep head bump, soft highs and flutter.
ToTape6.sound: Warm harmonics that project, tape-machine lows with a compressed quality, and flutter from subtle to wild.
ToTape6.use: A strong all-round tape sound on buss or tracks, with the final clipper acting as a loudenator.

controls.Head B: Head bump. Go gently past halfway: it adds a lot of low end.
controls.Flutter: Tape wobble. Defaults to 0.5 (adds small latency); 0 is off with zero latency.
controls.Output: Level after tape. Above 0 dB clips harder.
controls.Dry/Wet: Blend with dry. With flutter on, this makes a flanging effect.

FromTape.what: A minimalist, cleaner tape emulation: treble softening and an adjustable bass filter.
FromTape.sound: Transparent treble softening with a rounder, more open bass. No tape drive distortion; peaks pass through.
FromTape.use: Softening digital edge on channels or the 2-buss, or giving an over-limited mix some crest factor back. Light on CPU.

controls.Louder: Level pushed into the tape stage.
controls.Weight: Bass filter. Higher lets more bass through.
controls.Output: Output level. The bass cut can make it louder, so trim here.

TapeHack.what: A tape-saturation transfer function inspired by tape hysteresis research.
TapeHack.sound: Tape 'bark' on drums, forward heavy guitars, and livelier quiet tracks. Soft clip with extra peak energy.
TapeHack.use: Putting tape-style compression and peak energy on drums, guitars and mixes. Very light on CPU.

Tape.what: Simplified, all-purpose tape sound: Airwindows' personal 'mix into' output stage.
Tape.sound: Tape overdrive with a head bump, no flutter. Behaves well even stacked eight deep.
Tape.use: A simple tape stage on the output or buss.

controls.Bump: Head bump amount. Full is the original behaviour; default is 0.5.

IronOxideClassic2.what: Simple old-school tape sim, updated for high sample rates.
IronOxideClassic2.sound: Bandpassy, saturated and aggressively coloured, with a more organic tone at high rates.
IronOxideClassic2.use: Slamming tape on individual tracks for effect, at any sample rate.

controls.Tape Speed: Tape speed (ips), which shapes the bandpassy tone.

IronOxide5.what: The old-school, heavily coloured tape emulation, with flutter and noise.
IronOxide5.sound: Intense, bandpassy and saturated, with flutter and noise for grit.
IronOxide5.use: Slamming tape for effect on tracks. Setting Inv/Dry/Wet to inverted cuts a band while leaving the punch.

controls.Tape High: Upper cutoff of the tape band.
controls.Tape Low: Lower cutoff of the tape band.
controls.Inv/Dry/Wet: Inverted at one end, dry in the middle, wet at the other.

ToTape5.what: Airwindows' realistic analog tape emulation for mixing to tape in the box.
ToTape5.sound: Transparent and musical. The tape soaks up level without obvious tone change. Defaults are subtle.
ToTape5.use: Mix-buss or mastering tape. Small tweaks of 0.1 to 0.2 usually do it.

controls.Louder: Drive. Defaults to 0.25 because tape soaks up level; 0 removes the gain trim.
controls.Softer: Treble softening for an older tape-machine tone.
controls.Fatter: Head bump. Gives deep lows; turn Output down if you boost it.
controls.Flutter: Tape wobble. 0 is off; realistic levels are about 0.1.
controls.Dry/Wet: Blend with dry. Avoid with flutter, which makes a flange.

IronOxideClassic.what: The pure, simple early form of Iron Oxide: input, tape speed and output.
IronOxideClassic.sound: The clean, sweet original tone. No grit, flutter or noise.
IronOxideClassic.use: Cleaner tape slam on electronic or synthetic tones.

controls.Tape Speed: Tape speed (ips), which shapes the bandpassy tone.
